newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivory Coast to order study on duty-free zone.
newsitem.headline: Ivory Coast to order study on duty-free zone.

text.p: Ivory Coast is to conduct a feasibility study on setting up a duty-free zone in the economically depressed former trading port of Grand-Lahou.

A government statement, published in the government daily Fraternite Matin on Thursday, said President Henri Konan Bedie had called for the study on Grand-Lahou, which rose to prominence in the early days of French colonisation.

"Taking account of its geographical position and its history in our country since colonisation, the president... gave the government instructions to order a feasibility study to find out whether the Grand-Lahou region could become a regional and international port and airport free zone," it said.
Ivory Coast, the world's top cocoa producer, currently has two main ports, Abidjan, the commercial capital, and San Pedro in the south west.
Near neighbour Togo has enjoyed success with a free port. Neighbouring Ghana has made the ports of Tema and Takoradi into free ports in a bid to become a maritime hub for its landlocked neighbours.
The ports of Cotonou in Benin and Dakar in Senegal provide the other main competition in the region.
